items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: I sang with Duke right here at 49th and Broadway at the club called the Hollywood Club. And Duke was playing with Elmer Snowden's band.

ctx.x: Well, we had nice dressing rooms, because we had such beautiful costumes and things. Of course, we -- the stars always had to furnish their own clothes, but we paid a lot of money for our clothes, you know, and the chorus girls, they had a group of chorus girls. Let me see who worked there. A child -- let me see who was there with us. Louie and there was -- I think Pete, Peaches and Duke, three dancers, three of the greatest dancers you ever saw in your life, Pete, Peaches and Duke.

And they had beautiful girls -- this child Ginger. We called her Ginger. She later married Ray Robinson -- Edna Mae Robinson, but her name wasn't Robinson, naturally, before she married him, but she was a beautiful little brown skinned thing, and she was one of the chorus girls. And who -- oh, they had so many chorus girls. I don't remember.

items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Did the King attend the performance? [INTERVIEWEE] In London? Oh, yes. The King and Queen -- the old mother King and Queen. ... They came, and they -- I don't know whether they should have told us, but they did tell us.

ctx.x: Did the King attend the performance?

In London? Oh, yes. The King and Queen -- the old mother King and Queen. Now, listen -- Paul, bless his heart -- I love him so -- but you know what happened? They came, and they -- I don't know whether they should have told us, but they did tell us. And Paul came out tto sing Old Man River and went off pitch and stayed off.
